title: Pylon vs HubSpot Service Hub: which fits B2B support?
summary: Compare Pylon and HubSpot Service Hub on channels, agents, HubSpot CRM sync, MCP, and pricing. Keep HubSpot as your CRM, or stay on Service Hub.
body_markdown:
Choose Pylon when B2B customers reach you in Slack, Microsoft Teams, email, and chat, and you want agents that investigate issues with account and product context before your team opens them. Choose HubSpot Service Hub when support should live on the same platform as your HubSpot marketing and sales data, and customers mostly reach you by email, chat, forms, calling, WhatsApp, or Messenger.


You can keep HubSpot as your CRM and move support work to Pylon. That split is the decision this post is for. For a wider shortlist, see[HubSpot Service Hub alternatives for B2B support teams](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/hubspot-service-hub-alternatives) .


Disclosure: this post is published by Pylon. We stick to what each vendor says on its own public pages, checked Nov 12, 2026.

## What is the difference between Pylon and HubSpot Service Hub?


HubSpot Service Hub is HubSpot's customer service software. HubSpot describes it as connected to marketing and sales data on one customer platform, and it includes HubSpot's CRM ([Service Hub](https://www.hubspot.com/products/service) ). The help desk workspace and its channel connections are listed for Professional and Enterprise ([help desk channels](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/help-desk/choose-a-channel-to-connect-to-help-desk) ). It fits companies that already run marketing and sales on HubSpot and want tickets next to contacts and deals.


Pylon is the agentic support platform purpose-built for B2B. It's the help desk itself, with ticketing, SLAs, knowledge base, channels, and agents, not an AI layer on top of another tool ([Pylon Facts](https://www.usepylon.com/pylon-facts) ). Pylon is trusted by 1,800+ B2B customers.


## Can you keep HubSpot CRM and move support to Pylon?


Yes. Pylon connects to HubSpot with a service key you create in HubSpot, and the[HubSpot docs](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/integrations/crm/hubspot) cover what syncs:


- **Field sync** in either direction. Fields synced into Pylon work in views, triggers, and macros.
- **Activity sync.** Each day, Pylon summarizes customer conversations with AI and syncs the summary to the matching HubSpot account.
- **Contact sync.** When contact sync is turned on, Pylon adds anyone new who joins a customer channel to HubSpot and links them to the account.
- **Account details on the issue** , plus filtering issues by HubSpot tags and filtering broadcasts by HubSpot data.


One setup note from the docs: the Pylon card on HubSpot records, which powers account cards and Slack channel creation from HubSpot, isn't available with a service key connection.


Decide the boundary before you migrate. Which system owns accounts, contacts, and commercial fields? Which fields sync, and in which direction? Where does your team find the authoritative support history?


## How do Pylon agents compare with HubSpot Customer Agent?


Both platforms have a customer-facing agent and help for your team. They differ in where the agent's work starts.


HubSpot's Customer Agent answers customer questions, takes action in your CRM and connected tools, and hands off to your team with context. It needs Service Hub Professional or Enterprise and runs on HubSpot Credits ([Customer Agent](https://www.hubspot.com/products/artificial-intelligence/ai-customer-service-agent) ). HubSpot also offers Breeze Assistant for answers grounded in CRM data, and Agent Builder for custom agents ([Service Hub pricing](https://www.hubspot.com/pricing/service) ).


On Pylon, Support Agent resolves customer questions across every channel and brings in people when judgment is needed. Assist Agent investigates issues, uses your tools, and takes action with your team. Slack Agent answers and acts from Slack. Automations run on an event or schedule ([Pylon Facts](https://www.usepylon.com/pylon-facts) ). With Automations set to start on new issues, agents investigate issues before your team opens them, using context like past issues, account fields, connected codebases and logs, and MCP connectors ([Automations docs](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/agents/automations) ). Skills are reusable instructions that people and agents both run ([Skills docs](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/agents/skills) ).[Nexus](https://www.usepylon.com/nexus) describes the context, permissions, approvals, and traces behind that work.


The question for your team: do the hard issues need investigation across account history, product data, and engineering, or are most answers already in your knowledge base?


## How do Slack and Microsoft Teams compare?


This is often the deciding row for B2B teams.


HubSpot can sync help desk tickets to a Slack channel on Service Hub Professional and Enterprise. Your team can update ticket properties from Slack, and Slack thread replies sync back to a note on the ticket ([HubSpot help desk tickets in Slack](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/help-desk/sync-and-manage-help-desk-tickets-in-slack) ). HubSpot's custom channels can also connect marketplace messaging apps, with Slack among the examples ([custom channels](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/help-desk/connect-custom-channels-to-help-desk) ). Microsoft Teams isn't one of the help desk channel types HubSpot lists.


Pylon supports Slack Connect shared channels, Slack Community, and internal Slack channels on every plan, and Microsoft Teams and Google Chat on Advanced and Enterprise ([Pylon Facts](https://www.usepylon.com/pylon-facts) ). Agents and your team work together to investigate, resolve, and act on customer issues across those channels.


Material Security evaluated Zendesk and HubSpot Service Hub before choosing Pylon. Esther Disbot, Head of Product Support at Material Security, said: "Our customers love our conversational approach to the support experience. 90% of our customers prefer to receive support via Slack because it's so embedded in their everyday workflows. Pylon's tool made it possible for us to continue to offer Slack support in an efficient and flexible manner but it also made it possible for our customers to stay in their preferred communication platform of choice when they need to ask for help." Full story:[Why Material chose Pylon](https://www.usepylon.com/case-study/material) .


## How does pricing compare?


Pylon is seats plus agentic credits. Professional is $89 per seat per month and Advanced is $139 per seat per month on an annual contract. Enterprise is a custom quote. Agentic features run on credits, available pay-as-you-go or as a committed plan, and you can buy more in Pylon anytime. Assist Agent, Support Agent, Slack Agent, Automations, AI issue QA, and backtesting are "Credits required." Skills are included on every plan. Pylon doesn't charge per ticket ([Pylon pricing](https://www.usepylon.com/pricing) ).


HubSpot Service Hub is priced per seat by edition. Its pricing page lists a free plan for up to 2 users, Starter from $20 per seat per month, Professional from $100 per seat per month, and Enterprise from $150 per seat per month. HubSpot sometimes shows discounted prices for new customers. Professional and Enterprise each list a required one-time onboarding fee, $1,500 and $3,500 ([Service Hub pricing](https://www.hubspot.com/pricing/service) ). AI features run on HubSpot Credits. Paid plans include monthly credits that expire at month end, and you can add capacity packs or Pay-as-You-Go ([HubSpot Credits](https://www.hubspot.com/products/artificial-intelligence/credits) ). Customer Agent is priced per resolution. We don't publish HubSpot's credit rates here; check HubSpot's current pages when you model a deal.


A fair comparison puts your HubSpot renewal on one side and a Pylon quote sized to seats, credits, channels, and HubSpot sync on the other. Include onboarding, admin time, and AI usage at your real volume.


## When should you stay on HubSpot Service Hub?


Stay when support works best on the same platform as your HubSpot marketing and sales teams, your customers mostly reach you by email, chat, forms, calling, WhatsApp, or Messenger, and the answers to most questions live in your knowledge base. HubSpot lists a full help desk with routing, SLAs, knowledge base, surveys, and Customer Agent ([Service Hub pricing](https://www.hubspot.com/pricing/service) ). Moving tools isn't an improvement if it recreates the same setup somewhere else.


## When should you evaluate Pylon?


Evaluate Pylon when customers expect Slack Connect or Microsoft Teams as a support channel, when issues need investigation across account history, product data, and engineering, and when you want to keep HubSpot as the CRM.


Pylon's[HubSpot Service Hub migration guide](https://support.usepylon.com/articles/8446999228-data-migration-from-hubspot-service) maps users, companies to accounts, contacts, tickets and conversations to issues, and knowledge base categories, subcategories, and articles. Across 300+ migrations from Zendesk, Intercom, and Salesforce, 90% finished in under 2 months. Migrated tickets arrive closed. You can use Pylon's guided migration service for a one-time fee, or export from HubSpot and use Pylon's import API. Unpublished drafts and private knowledge base articles don't migrate with the tool. Validate a sample before you set a cutover date.


Both platforms also offer MCP servers, so your team can bring support and CRM data into[tools like Claude](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/connect-pylon-claude-mcp) . The Pylon MCP server is on every plan and accepts OAuth 2.0 or an API token ([Pylon MCP docs](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/integrations/pylon-mcp) ). HubSpot's remote MCP server is available to all HubSpot accounts and uses OAuth 2.1 with PKCE ([HubSpot developer changelog](https://developers.hubspot.com/changelog/remote-hubspot-mcp-server-is-now-generally-available) ).


Pylon is the help desk, not an add-on for Service Hub. If you only want an agent on top of HubSpot's help desk, Pylon isn't that product.

## FAQ


### What is the difference between Pylon and HubSpot Service Hub?


HubSpot Service Hub is HubSpot's customer service software, with help desk, Customer Agent, and service data on the same platform as HubSpot's marketing and sales tools. Pylon is the agentic support platform purpose-built for B2B: the full help desk, with agents, Slack Connect and Microsoft Teams channels, and account context.


### Can we keep HubSpot CRM and move support to Pylon?


Yes. Pylon's HubSpot integration documents field sync in either direction, optional contact sync, account details on the issue, and a daily AI summary of customer conversations synced to the matching HubSpot account. Decide which system owns each field and test your workflows before cutover.


### How much does each platform cost?


Pylon Professional is $89 per seat per month and Advanced is $139 per seat per month on an annual contract. Enterprise is a custom quote. Agentic features run on credits, available pay-as-you-go or as a committed plan, and you can buy more in Pylon anytime. HubSpot's Service Hub pricing page lists a free plan for up to 2 users, Starter from $20, Professional from $100, and Enterprise from $150 per seat per month, with AI features running on HubSpot Credits. Model both with your real seat count and AI usage.


### Does HubSpot Service Hub support Slack and Microsoft Teams?


HubSpot can sync help desk tickets to a Slack channel on Service Hub Professional and Enterprise, and its custom channels can connect marketplace messaging apps such as Slack. Microsoft Teams isn't one of the help desk channel types HubSpot lists. Pylon supports Slack Connect on every plan and Microsoft Teams on Advanced and Enterprise.


### Is Pylon an add-on for HubSpot Service Hub?


No. Pylon is the help desk itself. HubSpot can stay connected as your CRM while support runs in Pylon.


### Which should B2B support teams pick?


Our editorial pick for account-aware support in Slack, Microsoft Teams, email, and chat is Pylon. HubSpot Service Hub is the stronger fit when support should live on the same platform as HubSpot marketing and sales, and your customers mostly reach you by email, chat, forms, calling, WhatsApp, or Messenger.
